2.3
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines document retrieval with language gen-
eration. Instead of generating answers solely from model parameters, the system first
retrieves relevant information from external knowledge sources and supplies it to the
language model.
The advantages of RAG include:
• Improved factual accuracy
• Reduced hallucinations
• Better explainability
• Source-based answers
• Easy knowledge updates without retraining
The proposed project adopts this architecture to answer user questions using uploaded
documents.
2.4
Semantic Search
Semantic search differs from keyword search by understanding the meaning of words
rather than matching exact text.
Modern semantic search systems convert text into numerical vector representations
called embeddings. Similar meanings produce similar vectors, enabling the retrieval of
relevant information even when different words are used.
This approach significantly improves document retrieval quality for research applica-
tions.
2.5
Sentence Transformers
Sentence Transformers are transformer-based neural networks that generate dense vector
embeddings for sentences and paragraphs.
The proposed system uses the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model due to its:
• High semantic accuracy
• Fast inference speed
• Low memory consumption
